title: Retrieval quality on real public datasets
description: Finding 4 of BENCHMARK_STRATEGY.md's executive summary: the current retrieval-quality suite has a methodology problem BENCH-1 (EPIC-6) already diagnosed — Run A's scores were partly attributable to judge non-determinism, and a 50-question template-generated synthetic dataset "is explicitly NOT comparable to vendor-reported LongMemEval figures" per the existing report's own text. This epic is the fix: replace the synthetic dataset with the real, Apache-2.0 LongMemEval dataset and harness (BM-16), split the metric in two the way the strategy doc prescribes — deterministic IR metrics that need no LLM and can gate CI (BM-17), and LLM-judged end-to-end accuracy that runs offline/nightly and is never a merge gate (BM-18) — then re-run the SDK-configuration comparisons (hybrid vs. vector, consolidation on/off, reconciliation on/off) that EPIC-6's BENCH-3/BENCH-5 and EPIC-11's TRU-4 already explored, now on real data instead of a synthetic proxy (BM-19). This is distinct from EPIC-11's TRU-3 (adds a sycophancy category to the *existing* synthetic suite) and TRU-4 (re-runs the *existing* suite with the embedding provider swapped) — those stories audit and extend the current harness; this epic replaces its dataset entirely. Sequenced last on purpose per the strategy doc: retrieval quality is not least important, but it is the one workstream whose methodology is already known-broken, so it should be built on the pytest-native foundation from EPIC-13 rather than patched into the harness EPIC-13 is retiring. Depends on EPIC-13 (BM-3).
